negative_cases.missing_workstream: Canonical projection, authority, and generated operation inputs require WorkstreamKey; missing identity fails closed.
negative_cases.legacy_only: LegacyExactScopeCompatibilityInput validates only under its compatibility schema and cannot validate as WorkstreamAuthorityContext.
negative_cases.foreign_workstream: AttachmentKey ownership is checked against the requested WorkstreamKey; foreign nested owners are rejected.
negative_cases.foreign_continuity: ContinuityId is subordinate and mismatches with the AttachmentKey lineage are rejected.
negative_cases.foreign_workspace_binding: WorkspaceBindingId is subordinate and mismatches with the AttachmentKey binding are rejected.
negative_cases.foreign_projection_event_draft: Desktop projection, event, draft, profile-memory, HTTP transport, and Pi attachment paths compare generated identity rather than tab/CWD/latest-record fallbacks.
negative_cases.stale_revision_cursor: Existing projection/event/draft revision and cursor gates remain fail-closed and are covered by the Desktop runtime and contract tests.
negative_cases.empty_or_ineligible_contribution: Existing generated projection fixtures preserve omission diagnostics and deterministic adaptive layout behavior.

acceptance: Every canonical Result and Receipt schema carries or echoes the exact WorkstreamKey; Rust recomposition evidence/receipts and API receipts now emit the same generated identity chain.
Generated OpenAPI, operation registry, TypeScript client, validators, capability/parity artifacts, compatibility lock, and protocol handshake agree on Workstream authority metadata.

ScopeRef/ProjectRootKey is nested under WorkstreamKey; ContinuityId is optional and subordinate; AttachmentKey owns SessionId, InstanceId, and WorkspaceBindingId; runtime and WorkSurface identity are explicit.
Bounded Desktop consumers use generated identity types and generated validators rather than duplicate project_root/continuity authority DTOs.
Canonical HTTP query/body adapters and Mission Canvas core/API authority validation reject missing, malformed, foreign, or mismatched identity instead of inferring ownership.
The authentic Agent TUI remains a separate PTY-backed surface and does not become the Mission Canvas renderer.
